units.translation: But after recognizing the ruinous deception.
The god does not stand aloof from righteous deceit.
Homer used ἀπήτίμησε [he dishonored] (from ἀπατιμάω [to dishonor]) in Iliad 13, 113.
But I, thus dishonored by you.
Imperfect (as if from a present ἀπαυράω [to take away]: see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 1229).
[ἀπηύρω [he took away] in some copies Pr. 28 wrongly for έπηύρω [I took away] and this for ἐπηύρου [you took away]: see ἐπαυρίσκω [to enjoy, to reap the fruits of].]
For he took away the Ionians, the ship-fenced Ares of the Ionians.
to enjoy, to reap the fruits of
And I rushed unshod on winged chariot.
You might persuade if you persuade, but perhaps you would disobey.
which verse the interpolator fashioned from v. Ag. 426.
And he threatens the towers with terrible things, which may fortune not bring to pass.
Capaneus threatens, having prepared to do everything.
[He threatens these towers with things which may the god not bring to pass,]
to threaten such things as if she were prepared -.
and never cowering before harsh threats.
(with infinitive ἀπεῖναι [to be absent] and participle ἀπών [being absent]) I am absent.
And how did you revere any of the rulers when they were absent?
When judgment is absent, great harm occurs.
(with infinitive ἀπιέναι [to go away] and participle ἀπιών [going away]) I go away, but the present indicative having the meaning of the future, I shall go away.
But I shall go away beneath the earth to the darkness below.
But I shall go away to the house.
to forbid; to renounce, to fail
And no one, forbidding, keeps me from the halls of those pointed at by fingers.
He accomplished it, and the prayerful utterance from the father did not fail.
Thus from the Guelferbytanus copy for ἀπείργεται [he is kept away].
to keep the yoke of slavery away from this city.
and to keep away from the altars.
Why do you keep the suppliant away from the gates?
having no end, lacking an exit.
Similarly Pr. 1078 ἀπέραντον δίκτυον [an endless net].
Teach one who is inexperienced, guiding her.
I surround with an endless net, as if for fish.
Stand around in a circle in the boundless ambush, be gracious.

Bekk. Anecd. p. 421, 5 ἀπέλλητοι [uncontested ones]: ἀνταγωνισταί [rivals], thus Aeschylus (fr. 426). The gloss is suspected of corruption. For ἀνταγωνισταί [rivals] one would rather expect the adjective ἀνανταγώνιστοι [uncontested].
And do you think you dwell in a citadel free from grief?
the race of these just ones, free from grief.
And I forbid the untimely fates of men slain.
into the endless net of ruin.
The great mind of Zeus is not to be transgressed, impassable.
